column1: # crates/app/src/schematic/challenge/judge.rs
のとき、いちばん
# crates/app/src/schematic/lessons/digital.rs
90. MOSFET でロジックを組む (リング発振器で遅れを見る)
column2: 90. Logic from MOSFETs (see the delay in a ring oscillator)

column1: ロジック IC の中身は MOSFET の組み合わせです。CMOS インバータを 3 つ輪につないだリング発振器を過渡解析で動かし、ゲートの遅れ (伝搬遅延) が、つないだ先の容量を充放電する時間で決まることを確かめます
column2: Inside a logic IC are combinations of MOSFETs. Run a ring oscillator of 3 CMOS inverters connected in a loop with transient analysis, and confirm that a gate's delay (propagation delay) is set by the time to charge and discharge the capacitance it drives

column1: CMOS のインバータは、P チャネルの MOSFET (上、電源へ) と N チャネル (下、GND へ) のゲートを 1 つの入力にまとめたものです。入力が Low なら P がオンで出力は High、High なら N がオンで Low になります。片方は必ずオフなので、切り替わる瞬間以外は電源から GND へ電流が流れません (CMOS が電池で長く動く理由)。NAND は P を 2 つ並列、N を 2 つ直列にした形で、サンプル「CMOS の NAND」で見られます。インバータを奇数個 (3 つ) 輪にすると、どの点も「1 なら次は 0、その次は 1、その次は…」と自分の入力に戻ったとき逆になり、落ち着ける状態がありません。そのため信号がぐるぐる回り続けて発振します (リング発振器)。1 周で 2 回反転するので、周期は 2 × 段数 × 1 段の遅れ です。1 段の遅れは、出力が次の段の入力の容量 (C1〜C3 と、次のゲートの MOSFET そのものの容量) を、抵抗 R1〜R3 (長い配線や弱いゲートの代わり) を通して充放電する時間で決まります。だから、つなぐ先が多い (ファンアウト) ほど、配線が長いほど、デジタル回路は遅くなります。マイコンの最高クロックが決まるのも、同じ理由です。
column2: A CMOS inverter joins the gates of a P-channel MOSFET (top, to the supply) and an N-channel one (bottom, to GND) into one input. When the input is Low, P is on and the output is High; when High, N is on and the output is Low. One of them is always off, so no current flows from the supply to GND except at the moment of switching (why CMOS runs long on batteries). A NAND has 2 P in parallel and 2 N in series; see it in the sample "CMOS NAND". With an odd number (3) of inverters in a loop, every point comes back to its own input inverted ("if 1, the next is 0, the next 1, the next…"), so there is no state to settle in. The signal keeps going around and oscillates (a ring oscillator). It inverts twice per round, so the period is 2 × stages × one stage's delay. One stage's delay is set by the time the output takes to charge and discharge the next stage's input capacitance (C1–C3, plus the capacitance of the next gate's MOSFETs themselves) through resistors R1–R3 (standing in for long wiring or a weak gate). So the more inputs it drives (fan-out) and the longer the wiring, the slower a digital circuit gets. The same reason sets a microcontroller's top clock.

column1: MOSFET は、データシートの代表値に合わせた AO3400A・AO3401A のモデルです。IC の中の小さなトランジスタより、ゲートの容量がずっと大きい (約 1nF) ので、ここでは 1kΩ を入れて遅れを µs にしています。IC の中では同じことが ns より短い時間で起きます。
column2: The MOSFETs are AO3400A and AO3401A models fitted to the datasheet's typical values. Their gate capacitance (about 1nF) is far larger than the small transistors inside an IC, so here 1kΩ is added to make the delay µs. Inside an IC the same thing happens in less than ns.

column1: 電源の配線の抵抗やインダクタンス、切り替わる瞬間の電源の揺れは入れていません。実物では、貫通電流で電源が揺れ、パスコンが要ります。
column2: The resistance and inductance of the supply wiring, and the supply ripple at switching, are not included. In a real circuit, shoot-through current makes the supply ripple, and bypass capacitors are needed.

column1: 発振の始まりは、電源を入れた瞬間のわずかな差が育つことで決まります。シミュレーションでは計算の丸めの差で始まり、実物では雑音で始まるので、始まるまでの時間は実物と同じではありません。
column2: Oscillation starts when a tiny difference at the moment of power-on grows. In the simulation it starts from rounding differences in the calculation, and in a real circuit from noise, so the time until it starts is not the same as the real thing.

column1: 過渡解析で、3 つの点が順にずれて振れるのを見る
column2: Watch the 3 points swing one after another in transient analysis

column1: 「過渡解析を実行」を押し、N1・N2・N3 を選びます。電源が入ると (最初の 1µs)、3 つとも途中まで上がったあと、わずかな差が育って振れ始めます。N1 が下がると少し遅れて N2 が上がり、さらに遅れて N3 が下がる、と順にずれて約 5µs (約 200kHz) で回り続けます。周期 ÷ 6 (2 × 3 段) が 1 段の遅れ (約 0.85µs) です。
column2: Press "Run transient analysis" and pick N1, N2 and N3. When the supply turns on (the first 1µs), all three rise partway, then a tiny difference grows and they start to swing. When N1 falls, N2 rises a little later, and N3 falls later still; they keep going around one after another with a period of about 5µs (about 200kHz). The period ÷ 6 (2 × 3 stages) is one stage's delay (about 0.85µs).

column1: C1〜C3 を 2.2n にして、遅くなるのを見る
column2: Make C1–C3 2.2n and watch it slow down

column1: C1・C2・C3 を 100p から 2.2n に変え (つなぐ先のゲートが増えたつもり)、「過渡解析を実行」。周期が約 11µs (約 87kHz) に延びます。容量が 22 倍なのに 2 倍ほどにしか遅くならないのは、次の段の MOSFET のゲートそのものが約 1nF の負荷で、もともと 100p より大きかったからです。ゲートの数を増やすと遅くなるのは、このゲートの容量が増えるためです。
column2: Change C1, C2 and C3 from 100p to 2.2n (as if more gates were connected) and "Run transient analysis". The period grows to about 11µs (about 87kHz). The capacitance is 22 times larger but it is only about 2 times slower, because the next stage's MOSFET gate itself is a load of about 1nF, already larger than 100p. More gates make it slower because this gate capacitance grows.

column1: R1〜R3 を 220 にして、速くなるのを見る
column2: Make R1–R3 220 and watch it speed up

column1: R1・R2・R3 を 1k から 220 に下げ (強いゲート・短い配線のつもり)、「過渡解析を実行」。充放電が速くなるので、周期が短くなります。遅れは R × C で決まるので、抵抗を下げても容量を減らしても速くなります。IC では、トランジスタを大きくする (抵抗を下げる) と速くなる代わりに、ゲートが大きくなって前の段の負荷が増えるので、ちょうどよい大きさが決まります。
column2: Lower R1, R2 and R3 from 1k to 220 (as if the gates were strong and the wiring short) and "Run transient analysis". Charging and discharging get faster, so the period gets shorter. The delay is set by R × C, so lowering the resistance or reducing the capacitance both make it faster. In an IC, making a transistor larger (lower resistance) makes it faster, but the gate gets larger and loads the previous stage more, so there is a best size.

column1: # crates/cli/src/session.rs

Commands (one per line, '#' starts a comment; every answer is one JSON line)

 Schematic
  new                                   empty schematic
  open FILE.schjson / save FILE.schjson
  parts [WORDS]                         search the part library (name, category, description)
  part NAME                             pins (number + name) of a library part or a basic type (R C L D LED V I NPN)
  part import FILE [name=NAME] [subckt=SUB] [pins=A,B,..] [map=1,2,..] [package=PART]
                                        make a library part from a maker's SPICE .subckt (a plain-text file you downloaded):
                                        pins = the symbol's pin names in the subcircuit's node order, map = their pin numbers,
                                        package = a library part whose footprint is borrowed (default TL072, SOIC-8). Encrypted models are refused.
  lib [reload]                          the library folder and the number of parts; 'lib reload' reads it again (after part import or editing a file)
  libsync [apply=1] [parts=K1,U1]       the placed parts whose copy is older than the library (a model added or corrected since): listed, and
                                        brought up to date with apply=1 (place, reference and value kept; the copy's pins kept if the library's differ)
  add TYPE [VALUE] [as=REF] [unit=A] [rot=0..3] [at=X,Y]
        TYPE: R C L D LED V I NPN HEADER2 HEADER4 ... or a library part name (see 'parts')
  value REF VALUE                       change the value (a value with spaces, like PULSE(0 5 1m 1u), needs no quotes)
  nc REF.PIN [REF.PIN ...] [remove=1]    pins left unconnected on purpose (an unused output, a pin the data sheet says to leave open): ERC does not ask about them; no pins = the list
  pinnames REF NAME1,NAME2,...          the names of the pins of a pin header (F+,F-,SA,SB,GND): written beside its symbol and, with `board pinlabels`, on the silk (`-` clears)
  simonly REF [off]                     the part is only for the simulation (a test source, a stand-in for the device under test): it is left off the board and the bill of materials
  net NAME REF.PIN [REF.PIN ...]        connect pins by name; REF.PIN is the pin number or its name (any case; one part of a dual-use name like REFP1/AIN6 is enough)
                                        (GND pins of a part that share a name are all connected)
                                        The net named GND is the 0 V reference: every circuit needs one.
  remove REF
  list                                  parts, pins and the net of every pin (of the active sheet)
  sheet [add [NAME] | use N|NAME | name NAME | move REF.. to=N|NAME | tidy [all]]
                                        several sheets: no argument lists them; add makes an empty one (and makes it the active one);
                                        move sends parts (with the net labels on their pins) to another sheet; tidy packs the parts of the
                                        active sheet (or 'tidy all') into compact rows, so that the whole sheet fits one screen. Nets join across
                                        sheets by the same net label or power symbol; add / net / remove / list act on the active sheet
  tidy [REF ...]                        lay the sheet out again: signal left to right, supplies up, ground down (nets unchanged; with REFs only those parts, below the others)
  erc                                   electrical rule check (message + hint). 'ok' only says the command ran:
                                        read 'errors' (or run with --strict, which fails the script on an ERC error)
  spice                                 the SPICE netlist text
 Simulation
  dc [full] [temp=27] [probe=V(out),I(R1)]  operating point: node voltages, element currents (probe= returns only those; temp= every part at that temperature)
                                        (elements inside a library part's macro model are hidden unless 'full')
                                        'ratings' lists parts over / near their package power limit (like the app);
                                        'warnings' also flags an op-amp whose IN+ and IN- differ (saturated output)
                                        'solver' = how it was solved (strategy, iterations, seconds). A circuit with flip-flops lists them in 'memory':
                                        ic=NAME=1,NAME=0 sets their starting states. A latch built from gates has more than one answer:
                                        guess=NET=V,NET=V picks the one near those voltages (like .nodeset); 'dc states' also solves
                                        from other starting points and lists the nets that settle elsewhere ('other_states')
  tran TSTOP [TSTEP] [probe=V(out),I(R1)] [samples=6] [uic] [record=all|probes]
                                        starts from the DC operating point (a capacitor starts charged);
                                        add 'uic' to start from zero instead (step responses, oscillators)
                                        record=probes keeps only the probed signals (saves time and memory in a circuit with thousands of
                                        nodes; chosen by itself when the record would pass ten million values, record=all keeps everything)
                                        'ratings' / 'warnings' (second half of the run): resistor rms power, LED peak current,
                                        electrolytic ripple current, op-amp inputs that stay apart (saturation)
                                        settle=V(out) [from=20u] [tol=1e-2,1e-3,1e-4]: from the instant `from`, the time until the signal
                                        stays within each tolerance (a fraction of the step) of its final value; also the overshoot. ic= and guess= as in dc
 Maker SPICE models (the zips are the maker's own download, e.g. Murata 'SPICE netlist'; not shipped with the app)
  models [WORDS] [zip=PATH] [size=0603] [diel=X7R] [cmin=1u] [cmax=10u] [vmin=16]
                                        search the models by name; size (inch code), dielectric, capacitance and rating
                                        work for models a maker reader describes (Murata; Nippon Chemi-Con and Nichicon give capacitance and rating only). zip defaults to the ones added in the app.
                                        'models model=PN' prints the subcircuit (alias: murata)
 Models from data sheet readings
  fit FILE.fit.json [write] [dir=DIR]   an equivalent model (diode, BJT, MOSFET) from numbers and graph points read off a
                                        data sheet: answers the .model card, its notes and each reading next to the model's
                                        value (rows, error_pct); 'write' puts it into DIR/<part>.part.json (default: the library).
                                        The file's form: crates/part-lib/fits/*.fit.json (the bundled parts' readings)
  lineup FILE.pdf [series=F.elcap.json] [pick=PN,..|bundle|all] [write] [dir=DIR]
                                        an electrolytic capacitor's lineup table (one row per part number): lists the rows;
                                        'pick' makes those parts with the series' tables (crates/part-lib/elcaps/), 'write' saves
                                        them into DIR (default: the library)
 Several boards in one project
  project new FILE.ccproj               an empty project of several boards (written again if it is there)
  project add FILE.ccproj NAME [SCH.schjson] [board=B.pcbjson] [copies=N]
                                        a board into it: the session's circuit and board, or the files; a board of
                                        the same name is replaced (its links and 3D place kept)
  project link FILE.ccproj A.J4 B.P1 [cable=MM]
                                        two connectors joined (plugged, or by a cable of MM); answers the check's count
  project check FILE.ccproj             the links between the boards' connectors checked pin by pin (the same net names on both sides,
                                        power not on ground, pins not crossed, a signal not ending in an open pin)
  project bom FILE.ccproj OUT.csv       the parts of all boards counted together (times the copies of each board), one column per board
  project step FILE.ccproj OUT.step     the boards placed in 3D (stacked by their connectors in the app) as one STEP, and what collides
  project dc FILE.ccproj                the whole system's operating point: every linked pin's voltage on each side and the current through it
  project merge FILE.ccproj OUT.schjson the whole system as one schematic (designators R1_main, nets main.SDA, a 0 V source on every linked pin)
 3D body of a part
  shape [TEMPLATE|auto] part=NAME [DIM=mm ...] [dir=DIR] [max=TRIANGLES] [write]
                                        a body from a template (dc_jack, tact, relay, terminal; 'auto' picks by the footprint) as a
                                        SolidCraft script on the part's own pads; with SolidCraft installed it builds the body
                                        ('write' puts it into the part, max= thins it). 'shape' alone lists the templates and their dimensions
 Design help
  calc [KEY NUMBER ...]                 value calculators (led, divider, rc, regulator, buck, boost, opamp, ...): no
                                        arguments lists them with their inputs; the answer has the value, steps, cautions
  ac FSTART FSTOP [ppd=10] [probe=V(out)]
                                        frequency response (needs a source with an AC magnitude, e.g. value V1 "0 AC 1"):
                                        gain and phase per decade, -3 dB frequency, phase margin
  sweep REF START STOP [steps=11] [log=1] probe=V(out),I(R1)   (or sweep REF list=1,2,5)
  heat [temp=27] [top=10]               the DC point with every resistor warmed by its own power (a steady state): per part the power, rise, temperature and
                                        change of its value, and the nets that move because of it. thermal REF theta=K/W tc=ppm cth=J/K sets a part's heat resistance / coefficient / capacity; thermal link=Q1:RS1:150 keeps a heat resistance between two parts
  heattran TSTOP parts=Q1,RS1 [couple=Q1:RS1:300 (else the saved links)] [tstep=] [temp=27] [uic] [samples=8]
                                        a transient run whose power (I^2 R, I Vds) becomes temperatures over time: a pulse warms a part less than the
                                        steady state by its time constant (theta cth); couple=A:B:K/W lets two parts warm each other; a resistor's value follows its temperature
  sens probe=V(out) [step=1] [parts=R1,R2 | kinds=R,V,I,C,L] [top=15]
                                        sensitivity: moves each part's value by step % and says how far the probe moves (per_percent,
                                        elasticity), the biggest first; names the parts that decide an accuracy
                                        the DC point for a range of values of one part (a V source, R, C, L): one row per value; the part keeps its value
  worst NET [measure=dc|cutoff|rise|overshoot|settle|final] [tol_r=1] [tol_c=10] [tol_l=10] [tol_v=0] [temp=27] [f=10:1Meg] [tran=10m:10u] [top=8]
                                        worst case: the smallest and largest value of one result with every part at an end of its tolerance (%)
  breadboard                            the schematic on a solderless breadboard: the hole of each lead (a1..j30, rails 上+ 上− 下− 下+), the jumpers,
                                        the supplies off the board, and what the holes join that the schematic does not (problems)
  proto perf|strip [cols=N] [rows=N] [holes=1] [back=1] [svg=FILE.svg] [face=parts|copper]
                                        the schematic on a perfboard or a stripboard as the app lays it out: each part's holes and
                                        way on, the wires on top, the bare wires (or cuts), what to get, the check and the rules,
                                        the drawing to print (holes=1: mounting holes in the corners kept free)
  mount REF auto|direct|leaded|wired|lands
                                        how a part goes onto a board built by hand (wired: a chip with leads soldered on; lands:
                                        a chip on the copper side across two holes)
  pins [export=FILE.h] [check=FILE.ino]   the signals on the microcontroller board's pins (a part's pins or a header's pin names D13, A0,
                                        GPIO2): listed, written as a C header for Arduino (#define PIN_X 13), or a firmware's pin constants
                                        checked against the schematic (findings: a constant on another pin than the schematic has)
  firmware [set toolchain=arduino|pico|ice40|custom folder=DIR board= port= top= pcf= build=CMD flash=CMD]
                                        how the board's firmware is built and loaded (kept with the schematic): the commands of the outside
                                        tools (arduino-cli; cmake + picotool; yosys, nextpnr-ice40, icepack, iceprog; or your own) and the
                                        tools missing on this computer with where to get them
  firmware build|flash|all [dir=BASE]   runs them (the folder is relative to BASE, the current folder by default): the log, and where it
                                        stopped with hints for the errors met most
  adc REF [pos=AIN0] [neg=AIN1] [refp=REFP0] [refn=REFN0] [gain=1] [rate=20] [filter=sinc|low_latency] [chop=0|1]
                                        what an ADC (a part whose model has adc_bits) reads at the DC point: the code from the data sheet's
                                        ideal transfer function, the size of one step (lsb_v) and the code back as a voltage (reads_v); for a
                                        part with the data sheet's noise tables (ADS124S06/08), the noise at that data rate, filter and gain
                                        (rms and p-p, in volts and codes) and the effective and noise-free resolution in bits
  adcmeasure [NAME volts|ohms|amps plus=NET minus=NET | NAME part part=R7] at=V adc=U1 pos=AIN neg=AIN [gain=] [rate=] [filter=] [chop=]
             [when=K1,SW2,R5=10k] [refpos= refneg=]
                                        what the ADCs measure, one way per row, kept with the schematic: under its conditions (a latching relay
                                        set, a switch thrown, REF=VALUE a part's value), with a voltage, resistance or current of value at
                                        between plus and minus (or a part's own value: a sensor), the ADC's reading (a ratio with
                                        refpos/refneg); answers the input, the code, the slope, the noise in the measured unit (rms, p-p) and
                                        the digits that stay still. Without NAME every way is read; adcmeasure remove NAME
  timelog FILE.csv [temp=COLUMN]        a meter's log over time (a clock 10:00:01 or seconds, then readings; columns named by the header):
                                        per column the mean, min, max, p-p, standard deviation, drift per hour (a line fitted against
                                        time) and, against the temperature column, the temperature coefficient (per degree and ppm/degree)
  battery tran=STOP[:STEP] [from=T] [to=T] [node=NET v_min=V]
                                        how long the battery parts last: the average current over from..to of a transient run (default its second
                                        half; take whole periods of an intermittent load), the charge at which node falls under v_min, the hours
  budget [temp=25]                      the power budget of the supply rails at the DC point, as a tree (battery -> 5V -> 3V3): per rail its source,
                                        current, loads, rated current, headroom (what more it can give, and whether the rating, the heat or the rail
                                        above stops it), and a regulator's input, heat, temperature and efficiency
  inrush [r=0.1] [tstop=20m]            the current at power-on (the capacitors empty, each supply behind r ohms): per supply the peak, I^2t,
                                        how long it lasts, the DC current, the parts on the way against their rated current, an NTC value
  poweron [tol_r=5] [tol_v=0] [temp=25] [margin=1.5] [spread=on|off] [measured=12m] [supply=V1]
                                        first power-on of a built board: each supply's current at its printed values, the range a working
                                        board falls in (tolerances, data sheet min / max, self-heating), the current limit to set; measured= judges a reading
  mc NET [measure=dc|cutoff|rise|...] [runs=1000] [seed=1] [tol_r=1] [tol_c=10] [tol_l=10] [temp=27] [f=10:1Meg] [ppd=50] [tran=10m:10u] [lo=] [hi=]
                                        Monte Carlo: parts drawn at random inside their tolerance; mean, std, the 95 % range a few built
                                        boards should land in, a histogram, the parts that matter; lo=/hi= give the share inside the limits
  diagnose NET=V [NET=V ...] [rare] [top=8]
                                        troubleshooting: which single fault explains voltages measured on a circuit that does
                                        not work (every fault solved, ranked by fit and how often it happens), and where to measure next
  psrr NET FSTART FSTOP [supply=V1] [ppd=10]
                                        supply rejection: a 1 V ripple on one DC supply alone (the first one if not named), the share
                                        that reaches NET per decade (dB) and the rejection at 100 Hz, 1 kHz ...; the worst frequency
  nyquist PART FSTART FSTOP [ppd=10] [from=NET] [points=0]
                                        the loop gain (cut at PART, as 'loopgain') as a Nyquist chart: the crossovers as points of T, the point
                                        nearest to -1 and its distance |1+T| (0.5 or more is good), the sensitivity peak in dB
  locus PART FROM TO OUT FSTART FSTOP [in=NET] [n=15] [lin] [ppd=20]
                                        root locus: PART stepped from FROM to TO, the poles of V(OUT)/V(in) at each value (in Hz), the
                                        smallest damping, and the first value where a pole reaches the right half plane (oscillation)
  cmrr NET FSTART FSTOP [plus=V3] [minus=V4] [ppd=10] [tol_r=1] [runs=300]
                                        common-mode rejection of a difference amplifier: the + and - inputs' sources driven apart (Ad) and
                                        together (Acm), CMRR = |Ad/Acm| per decade; tol_r= draws the resistors and gives the spread (0 = none)
  noise OUT[,REF] FSTART FSTOP [ppd=10] [input=V1] [temp=27] [top=8]
                                        thermal / shot noise at net OUT (or the difference OUT,REF): rms over the band,
                                        density per decade, the biggest contributors; input=V1 also refers it to that source
  spec KIND TARGET LO HI [at=Hz]        pass / fail of the last dc / tran / ac answer against a range ('-' = no limit).
                                        'spec' alone lists the kinds (dc_voltage, tran_pp, ac_cutoff, ...)
                                        TARGET: dc_voltage = net name (MID); dc_current = part (D1, amps: 8m 12m);
                                        tran_* / ac_* = signal name as the answer shows it (V(OUT)); at= takes 1k, 10k ...
